instantiation.worst_case: Hello is the service's only RPC. After this change every request whose `name` is empty or whitespace — previously answered OK with "hello " — is refused with gRPC InvalidArgument (code 3). If the one deployed caller (workload `traffic` in namespace frontend, principal spiffe://cluster.local/ns/frontend/sa/frontend, cluster e1-dev, 3.2 rps, 100% success today per the rps query) ever sends a default/blank name, 100% of its calls to hello fail, permanently and immediately, with no retry recovery (the mesh retries only UNAVAILABLE). Two amplifiers make it worse than a one-line validation sounds: (a) the canary AnalysisTemplate `server-errors` (deploy/base/rollout.yaml) counts only code=~"Unknown|Internal|DataLoss|DeadlineExceeded", so a revision rejecting every request would pass analysis and promote to 100%; (b) the metrics stack has no alerting rules (discover.yaml metrics.is; ALERTS query empty) and Istio reports gRPC errors as HTTP response_code=200, so the failure is invisible on the mesh-level signals. Containment: internal only (both Services are ClusterIP), one authorized caller, one ready replica in e1-dev, ceiling 2; no persisted state. Blast radius is therefore one internal request path on one service in one dev cluster unless a prod cluster also runs it.

obligations.establish: The new rejection does not contradict the service's published contract: proto/hello/v1/hello.proto declares `string name = 1` with no required/validation option and documents Hello as answering "hello <name>"; confirm nothing in the repository's referenced docs (README.md, service.yaml, the proto comments, client/client.go doc block) states that a blank name is answered rather than refused, and note that the proto/comment was not updated to say name is now required. A contract or doc that promises an answer for an unset field, left unchanged, is a description-vs-behaviour mismatch.
obligations.evidence: proto/hello/v1/hello.proto (service + HelloRequest comments); README.md; service.yaml; client/client.go package doc; the diff of internal/handlers/hello_service.go

obligations.establish: No deployed caller sends an empty or whitespace-only name. The only caller measured is workload `traffic` (ns frontend, sa frontend) in e1-dev; service.yaml authorizes only smallStepGiantLeap/frontend for hello.v1.HelloService/Hello. Find the frontend repository's call site and show what it puts in HelloRequest.Name (a constant, a user field that can be blank, or an unset field). If it can send blank, those calls turn from OK into code 3 with no fallback.
obligations.evidence: org-finder: repository smallStepGiantLeap/frontend, the construction of hellov1.HelloRequest; cross-check with the measured callers query (sum by (cluster, source_workload, source_principal) (rate(istio_requests_total{destination_service_namespace="hello",reporter="destination"}[1h]))) and rps showing response_code=200 only

obligations.establish: The change relies on nothing new from the platform: no new dependency call, no new configuration key, secret, cloud resource or identity; google.golang.org/grpc (codes, status) and strings are already available to this module, and `make test` compiles and passes. Show this as the finding rather than assuming it.
obligations.evidence: go.mod of the root module; `go build ./... && go test -race -count=1 ./...` (Makefile target `test`) run in the mounted sandbox at 46ff747

obligations.establish: Mixed-version behaviour during the canary is tolerable: with steps 10% then 50% (deploy/base/rollout.yaml), the same blank-name request gets OK "hello " from stable pods and InvalidArgument from canary pods, and the mesh will not retry code 3 away (virtual-service route `idempotent`: retryOn connect-failure,refused-stream,unavailable). Establish that no caller breaks on this nondeterminism — i.e. the frontend either never sends blank names or treats an error as non-fatal — and that rollback is clean: the service persists nothing, writes no schema, reads no configuration format this change alters, so reverting the image restores the old behaviour exactly.
obligations.evidence: internal/handlers/hello_service.go (stateless handler, no storage); deploy/base/mesh/virtual-service.yaml retries block; deploy/base/rollout.yaml canary steps; frontend call-site error handling (org-finder)

obligations.establish: Show the change adds no load: it adds no outbound call and no fan-out, and returns earlier for rejected requests; and the rejection cannot multiply traffic, because Hello's mesh retry policy lists only connect-failure,refused-stream,unavailable and the canonical client sets no retry policy (only a 10s timeout in client.ServiceConfig). Confirm against current numbers (3.2 rps, inflight 0, p99 17ms, 1 ready replica, ceiling 2) that nothing about load changes.
obligations.evidence: internal/handlers/hello_service.go; deploy/base/mesh/virtual-service.yaml; client/client.go ServiceConfig; measured rps / inflight / p99_ms / ceiling queries already taken

obligations.establish: The new error path fails fast and cannot sustain a failure: InvalidArgument is returned before any work, is not in the mesh retryOn list for the `idempotent` route, and the client adds no retries — so a caller that starts getting code 3 sends no more load than before. Establish also that the frontend caller does not retry application errors in a loop (which would turn a permanent code 3 into a hot loop against hello, whose per-caller load is otherwise unlimited).
obligations.evidence: deploy/base/mesh/virtual-service.yaml (retries, both routes); client/client.go (no retry policy, 10s timeout); frontend call site and its retry/backoff handling (org-finder)

obligations.establish: The paved road exists and is used (owner query: all ReplicaSets in ns hello are owned by Rollout `hello`; Argo Rollouts canary 10%/5m -> 50%/5m with analysis from step 1), but establish whether any stage would actually catch this change being wrong: the AnalysisTemplate `server-errors` query filters code=~"Unknown|Internal|DataLoss|DeadlineExceeded", which excludes InvalidArgument, so a canary rejecting 100% of real requests passes analysis and promotes. Also establish the ladder: discover.yaml answers say there is no staging cluster (dev -> prod) and all measurements are from cluster e1-dev — confirm with the fleet whether a prod cluster runs hello, since that decides whether promotion of a blind canary reaches users.

obligations.establish: Show the property is unaffected: no new path, no new permission, no new identity; the rejection message is the fixed string "name is required" and does not echo or log the caller-supplied name, so no caller data leaves the service in an error. Confirm nothing in the changed code logs req.GetName().

obligations.establish: An operator can tell that hello started rejecting requests: confirm the platform stats handler records the handler's status code into vikrant_rpcs_handled_total{code="InvalidArgument"} and vikrant_unary_latency_seconds{code=...} for a unary error return (internal/platform/metrics/metrics.go, internal/platform/server/interceptors.go), so the discover.yaml `errors` query (code!="OK") would show it. Note explicitly whether the mesh-level signals would miss it: Istio reports gRPC failures with response_code=200, so the measured rps query would stay all-200 while every call fails.

obligations.establish: Establish what would actually page someone and whether the behaviour can be turned off without a deploy: the metrics stack is documented as having no alerting rules and the ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="hello"} query returned no data, and the handler has no flag or dynamic configuration gating the validation (cmd/hello/main.go flags are -drain-delay, -drain-spread, -shutdown-timeout only). If both hold, a 100%-InvalidArgument regression is silent and only revertible by a redeploy — say so with the two citations.

obligations.establish: CI would not be broken by the change, and would catch it being wrong. Specifically: the e2e probe calls Hello with an all-default message (e2e/probe/main.go: cc.Invoke with &emptypb.Empty{}), i.e. name="" — so every e2e call to hello now returns InvalidArgument. Establish that the `reach` matcher (e2e/run.sh ~line 227: CODE* not in PermissionDenied|Unavailable|DeadlineExceeded) and the drain `no-errors` matcher (tally's failure list in e2e/probe/main.go ~line 89: Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Internal, Unknown, Canceled) both still pass with code 3, and that the canary-promotion assertion still passes given the analysis query excludes InvalidArgument. If any of these would fail, the PR cannot merge/publish.

obligations.establish: Both new branches are tested at the repository's own standard: TestHelloRejectsEmptyName covers the whitespace case and TestHello covers trimming, and no other test in the repository still asserts the old "hello " answer for a blank name (notably client/client_test.go and internal/platform/server/*_test.go). Record that the previously-passing input "" -> "hello " was deliberately deleted from TestHello, so no test now pins the old contract — which is the intent, but means nothing in CI flags the behaviour change for callers.

summary: Business logic and tests are sound, and the change is low-risk today (no prod cluster exists, frontend has no real call site — only a synthetic traffic generator of unknown payload). But it ships with no safety net: the canary AnalysisTemplate's error-ratio query excludes InvalidArgument, and e2e's `reach`/`no-errors` matchers don't treat InvalidArgument as failure either — so a canary or a real caller failing 100% of Hello calls would pass CI and promote undetected, and nothing alerts on it. Fix the analysis query/e2e before trusting the paved road to catch this class of change.
